intro: A token identifier selects a learned vector; its numeric magnitude should not scale that vector.
task: Return embedding rows in the exact order of a supplied token-ID vector, preserving repeated tokens.
requirements: table is a nonempty finite (vocabulary, dimensions) matrix. token_ids is a nonempty vector of nonnegative integer values below the vocabulary size.
Return a NumPy matrix of shape (number of tokens, dimensions).
Repeated identifiers repeat rows. Output must be an independent copy so later edits cannot change the table.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

examples.name: Repeated tokens
examples.output:
[[5, 6], [1, 2], [5, 6]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: One token
examples.output:
[[-1.0, 0.5]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: Order matters
examples.output:
[[20], [10]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Use the token vector as row indices after validating its bounds and integrality.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Do not deduplicate token IDs; sequence order and multiplicity are meaningful.

explanation: An embedding table associates an integer vocabulary index with a dense feature vector. Lookup selects a row rather than performing arithmetic on the index.
Repeated tokens share parameters but occupy separate positions in the output sequence. Their outputs initially match because they read the same row.
Compare lookup with multiplying a one-hot matrix by the table. Explain why the direct indexing representation avoids allocating mostly zero entries.
